{{Quote|I've been monitoring you, Captain Rendar. You were correct to assume that following me would lead you to Boba Fett, but you are mistaken to believe you will claim the Rebels' reward for his location. You are outmatched.|IG-88D|<ref name="Shadows">[[Star Wars: Shadows of the Empire (video game)|''Star Wars: Shadows of the Empire'' video game]]</ref>}}
'''IG-88D''' was the fourth and last model of the [[IG-88 assassin droid/Legends|IG-88]] droid line. He and [[IG-88C/Legends|IG-88C]] were sentries on [[Mechis III/Legends|Mechis III]] after the four droids revolted against their creators.

==Biography==
===Early life===
{{Quote|Success on your mission, IG-88.''"<br />"''Success to yours, IG-72.|IG-72, and the response by all four IG-88s|<ref name="TIA">{{StoryCite|story=Therefore I Am: The Tale of IG-88|book=Tales of the Bounty Hunters}}</ref>}}
[[File:IG-88_activated.jpg|thumb|left|250px|The IG-88 droids are activated.]]
IG-88D was created on [[Halowan]] by the [[Holowan Mechanicals/Legends|Holowan Mechanicals]] Company in the [[Project Phlutdroid/Legends|Project Phlutdroid]]. After a droid of identical model called [[IG-88A/Legends|IG-88A]], turned against his biological creators, A then proceeded to activate and copy his programming into the other inactive droid's empty computer cores. A named the other droids by letter and by order of activation, and since he was last to be activated, IG-88A designated him IG-88D. All the assassin droids then continued to escape the laboratories they were created in, with the help of an assassin droid of similar model, called [[IG-72/Legends|IG-72]], who denied the option of joining them on their mission, but would help them escape. They then took a courier and escaped the planet, and set their sights on the foundry world of [[Mechis III/Legends|Mechis III]].<ref name="TIA" />

===Droid Revolution===
{{Quote|As there is a zero percentage probability that you will survive this encounter, I see no risk in informing you that I have tracked my esteemed competitor to the Zhar system, where he will soon lose Captain Solo to me. Now, I must control this interruption. You will detain me no further&hellip;|IG-88D, to Dash Rendar|<ref name="Shadows" />}}
The IG-88's managed to get all of the droids to kill the 73 organic [[Sentience/Legends|sentients]] on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] by slicing into the planet-wide defense grid. They then began reprogramming all the droids on Mechis III, so that they would have sentience programming, and obey their orders. Then they began to manufacture droids with embedded sentience programming, so that when IG-88 transmitted the signal, all the droids they manufactured would turn against their biological masters, thus taking over [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]]. Thus was the beginning of IG-88's [[Droid Revolution|droid rebellion]].<ref name="TIA" />

[[File:Dash_vs_IG-88D.jpg|thumb|right|250px|IG-88D battles [[Dash Rendar/Legends|Dash Rendar]] on [[Ord Mantell/Legends|Ord Mantell]].]]
With IG-88A impersonating the now-deceased administrator of Mechis III, and IG-88B acting as the bounty hunter "face" of the group, IG-88C and D were left to personally oversee the manufacturing of their plan and act as sentries for Mechis III. Soon after [[IG-88B/Legends|IG-88B]] was destroyed, C and D attacked [[Boba Fett/Legends|Boba Fett]] en route to [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure/Legends|Jabba Desilijic Tiure]] above [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]] to steal [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo's]] [[Carbonite/Legends|carbonite]] block in [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]] and avenge their lost "brother." C was destroyed by Fett without resistance, and as D was about to attack Fett, he was deceived by the bounty hunter, and the [[IG-2000/Legends|''IG-2000'']] was caught in a barrage of fire and crashed.<ref name="TIA" />

IG-88D survived the crash and managed to escape the notice of Boba Fett. He limped off to [[Ord Mantell/Legends|Ord Mantell]] in the main salvage plant to salvage whatever ship parts he needed. Before he was able to leave the planet, [[Dash Rendar/Legends|Dash Rendar]] tracked him there to get information on Fett's whereabouts. The [[Assassin droid/Legends|assassin droid]] managed to reprogram the plant's line of battle droids to [[Mission to Ord Mantell (Dash Rendar)|attack]] Rendar, but he managed to get through on a [[Hovertrain/Legends|hover train]] system. It was IG-88D that revealed to Rendar that Fett was on his way to the [[Imperial Enclave]] on [[Gall/Legends|Gall]]. The two had a firefight in the main plant, and IG-88D was ultimately taken out by Dash. The intel received was used to organize the [[Battle of Gall]].

==Personality and traits==
{{Quote|Surrender your prisoner and you have a thirty percent probability of surviving this encounter. I am far more capable of withstanding the gravometric ''[sic]'' pressures than you. This tactic has a zero probability of success.|IG-88D, Boba Fett|<ref name="TIA" />}}
A calculating assassin droid, IG-88D was confident in his ability to defeat adversaries such as Boba Fett.<ref name="TIA" />

==Skills and abilities==
{{Quote|We will go to intercept Boba Fett. Regardless of his skill, this biological will never survive an encounter with two assassin droids.''"<br />"''Go. I will stay here to complete the Death Star mission. You eliminate Boba Fett.|IG-88C and IG-88D, and IG-88A|<ref name="TIA" />}}
[[File:RendarsWrath .jpg|thumb|left|250px|IG-88 hunting Dash Rendar]]
IG-88D was able to calculate probabilities and, in collaboration with IG-88C, was able to deduce Boba Fett's location without the aid of a tracking device.<ref name="TIA" />

==Equipment==
{{Quote|Programming. We installed two sensors aboard Boba Fett's ship.''"<br />"''We could trigger the dormant tracer and locate where he has gone.''"<br />"''Correct. But if Fett has Han Solo, we already know where he will go.|IG-88s C and D|<ref name="TIA" />}}
IG-88D possessed a starship identical to the original ''IG-2000''. He and IG-88C had access to sensors equipped with trackers installed aboard Boba Fett's starship, ''Slave I''.<ref name="TIA" />

==Behind the scenes==
In the 1997 PC release of [[Star Wars: Shadows of the Empire (video game)|''Star Wars: Shadows of the Empire'']], IG-88D was voiced by [[Nick Tate]].
